00.1 / Macro logic frame

Why these fifteen — the frame that ties every pursuit together

The overall frame, stated once. Each pursuit card below references it.

END STATE
The MPJV has expanded its footprint at Soto Cano into the other important BOS and logistics work of Central and South America — the Caribbean CSLs, HA/DR staging, and the Southern Spear-driven logistics demand across the SOUTHCOM AOR. The other lines of effort support that expansion with bench depth, past performance, and cash flow.
▲  constrained by
BINDING CONSTRAINT
Neither RMGS nor Versar holds an EAGLE II BOA or a LOGCAP V prime contract. Direct order access exists only through WEXMAC. Every EAGLE and LOGCAP pursuit on this page therefore runs one of three lanes: (1) vehicle-steering — convince the contracting officer during market research that the requirement is commercial services and can be competed through WEXMAC; (2) teaming — subcontract or CTA with a vehicle holder (a second mentor-protégé JV is unavailable while the Versar MP relationship stands); (3) alternative pathways — and these open wide the moment the scope is determined commercial. Base operations, maintenance, supply, transportation, and facilities support are commercial services under FAR 2.101, which unlocks FAR Part 12 streamlined acquisition, FAR 8.4 GSA MAS orders and BPAs, FAR 13.5 simplified procedures for commercial products/services (to $7.5M, $15M in contingency), Commercial Solutions Openings, and 8(a) direct awards — each a legal route around the vehicle the JV doesn't hold. The commerciality determination is what opens these routes. The constraint may also change: the government is considering consolidating EAGLE under LOGCAP VI as a small-business set-aside MATOC (~2027) — a seat the MPJV intends to compete for. Winning a seat would convert LOE 3 from steering and teaming into direct prime standing, and the CONUS pursuits below build qualifications for that bid.

▲  resting on
CAPTURE STRATEGY
The administration's demand signals — the border and detention buildout at home, the Southern Spear ISR surge in the hemisphere, the eastern-flank permanence in Europe, the 2027 readiness window in the Pacific, and the post-strike hardening bill in the Gulf — all convert into base-operations and sustainment dollars on vehicles where the incumbents are large primes and the buyer is under small-business pressure. The JV does not need to displace KBR, V2X, or Amentum head-on, and it does not need to hold their vehicles. Because the scope is largely commercial, requirements can move to vehicles the JV already holds (WEXMAC, MAS, a set-aside, a CSO) when the contracting officer has a defensible basis for the move. The capture task on each pursuit is to build that basis. Each pursuit either supports the hemispheric campaign directly or builds the past performance and bench that sustain it.
Standing assumptions: FPDS periods of performance drive timing (verified monthly); neither JV partner holds EAGLE II BOA or LOGCAP V prime standing — every EAGLE/LOGCAP pursuit runs through steering, teaming, or commercial pathways until that changes; disrupted windows (court injunctions, protests) reopen — they don't close.
00.2 / Strategic environment

Administration posture by theater and the demand it creates

Distilled from the AOR intelligence briefs on the Opportunity Map (posture statements, NATO summit outcomes, strike reporting, open-source contract intelligence). Each card links to the full brief. Every posture claim on this page is a [SIGNAL · as of 2026-07] — the same discipline as the standing flags: signals expire, re-verify at each capture gate.

NORTHCOM FULL BRIEF ↗

The border campaign, National Defense Areas, and the detention-operations buildout are the administration's signature domestic effort; Golden Dome and Arctic posture add installation demand in Alaska. Volt Typhoon pre-positioning inside power, water, port, and rail systems puts installation resilience — and the contractors who deliver it — on the critical path. [SIGNAL · 2026-07] Feeds the EAGLE LRC set (Benning, Bragg, Carson) and Wainwright.

SOUTHCOM FULL BRIEF ↗

Operation Southern Spear has surged ISR through the Caribbean CSLs; cartels carry FTO designations; Venezuela-transition and Panama Canal planning both assume forward logistics. Disaster diplomacy (Hurricane Melissa response) keeps HA/DR staging live. The CSLs are now the highest-tempo small bases in the hemisphere. [SIGNAL · 2026-07] Feeds the CSL bundle.

EUCOM FULL BRIEF ↗

The administration is pushing Europeanization of conventional defense while keeping the eastern flank built out — Eastern Sentry after repeated drone incursions, the seabed war in the Baltic, and Ukraine assistance restructured through the PURL logistics chain. Burden-shift scrutiny of legacy LOGCAP sites cuts both ways: pressure on cost, opening for leaner small-business models. [SIGNAL · 2026-07] Feeds Rota, Incirlik, Grafenwöhr, and Bondsteel — Rota being the Atlantic gateway, where burden-shift friction with Madrid hasn't touched US-funded operations contracts.

CENTCOM FULL BRIEF ↗

The Twelve-Day War and the March 2026 Iranian missile/UAS strikes (16+ sites damaged across 8 countries) left a $25–50B hardening-and-dispersal bill not yet in the FY27 budget, alongside Iraq/Syria retrograde and Gaza stabilization logistics. Hardening funds carry base-ops and environmental scope with them. [SIGNAL · 2026-07] Feeds Incirlik (Türkiye seam) and raises Rota's dispersal-throughput role.

INDOPACOM FULL BRIEF ↗

The 2027 readiness window drives distributed sustainment: prepositioned stocks, island infrastructure, EDCA sites in the Philippines, and the Guam buildout. Care of supplies in storage is treated as a readiness metric. [SIGNAL · 2026-07] Feeds the APS re-compete, the Korea and Okinawa surge lanes, EDCA site logistics, Darwin rotation support, and the Guam buildout.

AFRICOM & NON-DOD FULL BRIEF ↗

A record strike campaign in Somalia, the Horn buildout, West Africa re-entry, and the Lobito minerals corridor keep austere sustainment demand alive. Outside DoD, State INL's Ecuador judicial-security requirement (Sol. RFI001J, award est. 09/2026) is the JV's cleanest non-DoD entry — Ecuador country brief ↗. [SIGNAL · 2026-07] Feeds LOE 4.

00.3 / The pursuit groups

Fifteen pursuits in three groups — contract, strategy, and the logic behind each

Organized by engagement type, in priority order: Group A, Western Hemisphere (natural extensions from Soto Cano — the end-state pursuits, and prime bids in their own right); Group B, prime pursuits (direct WEXMAC orders or a viable non-traditional / commercial authority); Group C, best combined fit (the capability record carries the offer; access via teaming or steering). Within each group, theater priority orders the cards. Every card links to its full record, its FPDS lineage, and its pin on the Opportunity Map.

00.4 / Sequencing

The order of operations

NOW — Q3 2026
Benning teaming (RFP live) and the Rota bid/no-bid (PoP ends 2026-12) are immediate actions. Simultaneously: CSL Curaçao/Aruba site visit and customer-sentiment soundings before the RFP drops; APS-3/4 teaming agreement while the re-competition is still forming; Camp Humphreys WEXMAC surge proposal ahead of the next UFS cycle (capture window open); Darwin order positioning before the next MRF-D rotation boundary; Grafenwöhr WEXMAC surge-lane positioning ahead of the 2026-11 observed task-order horizon.
Q4 2026 — Q2 2027
Bragg teaming and the Carson steering campaign use the capture infrastructure built for Benning: one pipeline serving three pursuits. The Rota proposal-and-award cycle runs here; Incirlik/UABOS carve-out white papers land while the $25–50B hardening bill is being marked up.
2027 — FY28
The LOGCAP VI SB MATOC solicitation — the vehicle-acquisition bid, built on the EAGLE teaming record. Philippines EDCA, Kadena, and Guam order cycles mature (capture by 2027-03); Wainwright and Bondsteel recompete decisions land in the same window; Powidz drops to a watch item unless a surge lane opens first.
CONTINUOUS

03 / FPDS universe

WEXMAC · LOGCAP · similar-scope task orders, from the award record

Every award in the USAspending extract that sits under a WEXMAC or LOGCAP umbrella (tagged by parent IDIQ), plus every award in a similar scope — base ops, facilities, fuels, transport, air terminal, port, food service, security, staffing, engineering, environmental — mapped to the combined capability areas by NAICS. Dates here are actual FPDS periods of performance, the collection requirement the standing flags call for. Umbrella coverage was completed with an IDV-children pull of the 27 WEXMAC/LOGCAP parent contracts with observed task orders — every filed order, CONUS and OCONUS. Note: NAVSUP awarded WEXMAC 2.0 to 87 firms; seats with no filed task orders yet produce no FPDS records and are not listed here.

04 / Forecast

Contract start / end timeline

All records with a published or vehicle-bounded end date, 2016–2032; records with no date signal at all are tracked on the target board only. Gold line = today; the gold diamond on each bar is the capture-start point (end date minus 12 months; 9-month floor) — the date ground-truth recon must begin. The shorter clock reflects the JV's ability to transact quickly on a held vehicle. Solid bars have a published end date. Dashed bars have no published task-order end date, so they are bounded by the vehicle ceiling: LOGCAP V PoP ends Mar 2, 2030; WEXMAC 2.0 base ordering ends Dec 2029 (option to 2034). Vehicle-ceiling estimates are marked EST and are a worst case. Where the FPDS universe (section 03) holds a matched task order, the ceiling estimate is replaced by the observed FPDS end date — tagged FPDS and drawn solid.

09 / Standing flags — never silently included
[UNVERIFIED] Price / wrap competitiveness — no rate data in either corpus. Price-to-win before any gate. The Soto Cano price win does not transfer automatically.
[GAP] Transportation, food service / DFAC, and executed HA-DR surge — no records in either corpus. Teaming requirements on any TO where these dominate.
[GATE] No EAGLE II BOA (watch SAM.gov for on-ramp). No LOGCAP V position — "dual LOGCAP + WEXMAC reach" stays retired.
[UNVERIFIED] NAICS 561210 registration — confirm in SAM before any BOS prime bid.
[COLLECT] Records with no published task-order end date carry an EST end bounded by the vehicle ceiling (LOGCAP V PoP ends Mar 2, 2030; WEXMAC 2.0 base ordering ends Dec 2029, option to 2034). EST is a latest-possible date — the real PoP is a collection requirement (FPDS/GovWin) before B&P commitment. Where a matched task order exists in the embedded FPDS universe, the observed end date is used instead (tagged FPDS); confirm PIID lineage before gating.
[SIGNAL] Disrupted records (TITUS conversions, ICE detention orders) reflect court/exec actions as of the map snapshot — perishable; re-verify.
[FPDS] Universe dates are task-order periods of performance as filed in the USAspending export (2026-07-10). WEXMAC seat-family tags are inferred from parent IDIQ families; EAGLE task orders come from a USAspending API pull (2026-07-11, CONUS Army NAICS 561210, keyword-tagged EAGLE/LRC) and may not be exhaustive. Verify PIID lineage in FPDS-NG/GovWin before committing B&P.
